posts.text:
BREAKING: US imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors surged +$12.1 billion in September, to a record $86.9 billion.

This marks the 2nd-largest monthly increase in history, following the record +$14.7 billion increase in July 2026.

Since the start of 2024, imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors have more than quadrupled.

YoY, these imports rose +151%, the largest YoY increase on record, compared with peak annual growth of just +34% during the 2000 Dot-Com Boom.

Based on September's figures, these imports are now running at an annualized rate above $1.0 trillion for the first time.

US demand for technology hardware is exploding.

Thursday was a historic session in the US options market:

US put option trading volume on CBOE surged to a record 11.23 million contracts on Thursday.

This surpassed the previous all-time high of 10.22 million contracts set on April 4th, 2025.

As a result, the 20-day average of put option volume rose to ~7 million contracts, near its highest on record.

By comparison, the 20-day average oscillated around 4 million contracts in 2022.

8 of the 10 highest daily put option volume readings have occurred in 2026.

We are seeing unprecedented options activity right now.

posts.text:
History says last week's drop was a buying opportunity.

On Thursday, the S&P 500 declined -4.4%, its largest daily drop since April 2025.

Before that day, the index recorded 56 one-day declines of at least -4.0% since 1952.

Following such drops, the S&P 500 has gained +1.0% on average over the next week.

By comparison, its average weekly return across all periods has been +0.2%.

Over the next month, the index has averaged a gain of +2.0%, compared with +0.8% across all periods.

Over the following 3 months, the S&P 500 has averaged +6.7%, more than triple the historical average of +2.2%.

History suggests the market is set for a meaningful rebound.

posts.text:
The global rate hike cycle is accelerating:

~45% of global central banks have raised interest rates over the last 3 months, the largest total in 3 years.

This proportion has surged +40 percentage points since March.

By comparison, between 2024 and March 2026, more central banks were cutting rates than raising them.

Furthermore, global central banks have delivered 42 rate hikes over the last 6 months, the largest number since late 2023.

This figure has quadrupled over the last 7 months and is comparable to the rate hike cycle seen in 2019.

The global monetary tightening cycle is gaining momentum.

BREAKING: The Fed’s balance sheet expanded +$3 billion in the week ending November 4th, to $6.75 trillion, its 3rd-highest level since mid-March 2025.

Total assets have surged +$212 billion since the December 2025 low.

Over this period, Treasury holdings have risen +$390 billion, to $4.58 trillion, their highest since March 2024.

At the same time, holdings of Mortgage-Backed Securities have declined -$170 billion, to $1.88 trillion, their lowest since June 2020.

The Fed's balance sheet stands now +$2.99 trillion, or +80%, above pre-pandemic levels.

The Fed's balance sheet is growing again.
